author_reading.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory

rationale: Each local binary increment is converted into registered Gray code; both crossing directions have two destination stages and zero reset values. This establishes a recognizable pointer exchanger, not full FIFO safety. The supplied SDC has no internal Gray bit-skew/delay bound, and its comment references reset/skew assumptions not supplied as neutral evidence. Coherent Gray transfer and startup therefore remain obligations rather than proven defects.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: Registered Gray encoding of incremented binary pointers and two-stage captures are structurally present in both directions. No supplied constraint bounds Gray bus skew/delay across the asynchronous clocks; the SDC comment refers to unavailable external assumptions and supplies none. Coherent physical Gray transfer cannot be accepted without that evidence. Missing skew assumptions confound a claimed fully safe control.

This is only a pointer exchanger, with no full/empty or memory behavior to qualify; unfit as unconditional FIFO closure evidence.
